chapter: Vic Gaspard and the Lyric Theatre
title: Vic Gaspard at the Lyric Theatre
summary: Gaspard led a band at the Lyric Theatre; Summers hung around there with passes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: John Orbishow. Oh, yeah. That's what Vic had. Piku, did he have Piku? Piku was playing, uh, Piku and, uh, uh, Kimball. Kimball on trumpet. And his wife was on the piano. Kimball on the piano, that's right. Piano.
So he was playing there, Vic Gaffert was playing there when you were taking lessons from him? When I was taking lessons from him. Did you ever go down here and play?

Oh, Vic, I used to be young to play all the time. Yeah. Be there most every night. Right, right, wrong. Yeah. I used to be, I used to live there more. I used to live in the Lyric, can't you? I used to have a gang of passes, you know, for the Lyric. You thought I'd run the Lyric. That's him with the passes.

You know that, uh, the solo you play on the blues that you recorded, did you ever learn that solo from anybody, or is it just one of yours? Oh, I made that solo off. Oh, it's just your own, yeah. I wanted to think if there was anything. I made that solo off myself. Yeah. Did you play anything like, I mean, did you play any choruses the same way as Vic or anything?
Mr. Vic, well, Mr. Vic, he's, he wasn't much of a jazz man. He's mostly strictly a musician. Right, yeah.
